title: Entitlement activation playbook and audit schema
content:
Purpose:

This playbook documents the entitlement activation lifecycle (request -> approve -> activate -> evidence capture -> review) for RBAC v2 roles across hosting tiers (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private). It standardizes short-lived access patterns, required approvals, audit logging schema, and SIEM export mapping so that Evidence Automation can reliably prove compliance for audits.

Scope:
- Applies to human and service-account elevated access requests that change runtime configuration, tenant isolation, or access customer data.
- Environments: hosted (multi-tenant Redwood control plane), dedicated (reserved capacity with tenant scoping), private (VPC/on-prem boxed control plane).
- Not in scope: standard read-only tickets for dashboards unless they escalate to write/exec.

Glossary (short):
- Entitlement: a role or capability (e.g., tenant-admin, deployment-manager, key-rotator).
- JIT (Just-in-Time): temporary access issued for a timebox with automated revocation.
- Evidence record: structured artifact stored in Evidence DB/S3 that proves activation and approval chain.
- Activation ID: unique UUID assigned to a temporary entitlement instance.

High-level lifecycle (single-line):
1) Request -> 2) Triage -> 3) Approval -> 4) Issue JIT creds / grant role -> 5) Audit & evidence capture -> 6) Auto-revoke + post-mortem (if required)

Operational rules by hosting tier:
- Hosted API:
  - Tenant-admin and infra-scoped changes require 2 approvers: one security approver (security-and-compliance) + one product/owner approver.
  - JIT window default: 2 hours; max 8 hours with exec exception.
  - All activations must include: purpose, runbook link, Instance IDs, and justification.

- Dedicated:
  - Access that crosses tenant boundaries (e.g., migration, mass-config) requires 3 approvers: security, infra-owner, solutions-eng.
  - Default JIT window: 4 hours; max 24 hours only with written customer approval (logged).
  - When enabling SSH into dedicated nodes, ephemeral bastion tokens must be used and session recordings enabled.

- Private (VPC/on-prem):
  - Entitlements normally provisioned by customer-managed tooling. Redwood support engages only via documented SOW.
  - If Redwood employees need access, a signed customer-approved request + 3rd-party attestation is required.
  - Default JIT window: 8 hours; no automatic extension without customer sign-off.

Role matrix (RBAC v2 — condensed):
Columns: role | primary-capabilities | default-scope | approval-tier | jito-default-hours
- platform-admin | cluster-config, kernel-selection, model-routing | global | exec + security | 1
- deployment-manager | rollout, canary, rollback | product-owned route | product-owner | 2
- tenant-admin | tenant config, data-scope, keys (read/write) | tenant | tenant-owner | 2
- service-account:ops | automation run, metrics-push | system | infra-owner | 24 (service tokens rotated automatically)
- read-only-audit | logs, dashboards | scoped | security | NA
- auditor | read-only + export | broad-scope for audit | security -> compliance lead | NA

Approval flow (detailed):
1) Request created in Jira (SEC-AUTH template) or via Self-Serve portal. Request must include: reason, scope (resources), requested duration, runbook link, customer impact assessment.
2) Triage bot assigns risk level (low/medium/high) based on scope and recent incidents.
3) Approver set determined by role matrix and hosting tier. Approvers receive Slack + email.
4) Approver signs via Slack approval action (logged) or via JIRA. Approvals must include short justification.
5) Automation issues JIT credentials (temporary role binding) and creates an Evidence record with Activation ID.
6) On expiry, automation revokes binding and appends revocation evidence; if activity above threshold during window, a post-activation review is created.

Evidence capture specification:
Each activation produces a single structured evidence record (JSON) stored in the Evidence Bucket with path pattern: /evidence/{year}/{month}/{activation-id}.json
Required fields (every record):
- activation_id: string (uuid)
- requester: string (email)
- approvers: list of strings (emails)
- role: string
- scope: string (resource identifiers)
- host_tier: string (hosted|dedicated|private)
- requested_duration_minutes: integer-as-string
- issued_at: rfc3339 string
- expires_at: rfc3339 string
- justification: string
- runbook_link: string (optional but recommended)
- evidence_refs: list of strings (session recordings, SSH session id, console logs)
- authorization_flow_id: string (JIRA key or portal id)
- automated_checks: list of strings (pre-activation checks executed)
- post_actions: list of strings (revocation event ids, review ticket ids)

Note: The JSON above is serialized as plain text and must be checksum-signed (sha256) at write time; the checksum value is stored with the S3 object's metadata and exported to SIEM.

Audit log schema (production events for SIEM ingest):
Field name | type | description | example
- event_ts | timestamp | when event occurred | 2026-01-15T14:23:07Z
- event_type | string | high level event (activation_request|approval|issued|revoked|suspicious_activity) | approval
- activation_id | string | Activation UUID | 6b8f5f2e-1f7c-4d8e-bb90-ae3c1c9f7f14
- requester | string | user principal | aisha.patel@redwood.ai
- approver | string | approver principal (if applicable) | marcus.nguyen@redwood.ai
- role | string | role name granted | tenant-admin
- scope | string | resource identifiers | tenant:acme-corp / cluster:eu-west-1-1
- host_tier | string | hosted|dedicated|private | dedicated
- approval_result | string | approved|denied|escalated | approved
- justification | string | short justification text | emergency migration to patch CVE
- evidence_ref | string | S3 path or session id | s3://evidence/2026/01/6b8f5f2e.json
- checksum | string | sha256 of evidence payload | abc...123
- triggered_by_automation | boolean-as-string | "true" or "false" | "true"
- source_ip | string | origin of activation request | 54.201.10.32
- user_agent | string | client that requested | portal/v1

SIEM export mapping (examples):
- Splunk raw event index: redwood_entitlements
  - sourcetype: redwood:entitlement:activation
  - fields mapped: activation_id -> activation_id, event_ts -> _time, role -> role, host_tier -> host_tier, checksum -> evidence_checksum
- Datadog: use logs with attributes and attach facets for role, host_tier, approval_result. Use tag entitlement.activation_id:{activation_id} for correlation.
- Elastic/ELK: index alias redwood-entitlements-prod, map activation_id to keyword, event_ts to @timestamp, approvers to keyword array.

Sample SIEM saved query (Splunk-style):
index=redwood_entitlements earliest=-24h@h | stats count by role, approval_result | where approval_result="denied"

Automated evidence pipeline (implementation pattern):
1) Trigger: Portal or Jira webhook posts to Evidence-Ingest service with request payload.
2) Collector: Evidence-Ingest validates request, runs pre-checks (is user 2FA enabled? is request scope allowed?) and assigns risk score.
3) Enrichment: Collector fetches related artifacts (session ids, PR links, runbook snapshot) and composes evidence JSON.
4) Sign & Store: Evidence JSON is SHA256 signed and uploaded to S3 with retention tags; metadata written to Evidence DB (Dynamo).
5) SIEM Forward: Lambda (or Log-Forwarder) pushes event envelope to Splunk/Datadog/Elastic with required mappings and tags.
6) Orchestration: Orchestrator schedules revocation job at expires_at and triggers review if thresholds breached.

Example policy template snippets (condensed):
-- Hosted API (IAM policy pseudo-JSON) --
{
  "Version": "2024-01-01",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["redwood:DeployModel","redwood:ReadMetrics"], "Resource": "arn:redwood:tenant:${tenant_id}:*", "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"redwood:Role": "deployment-manager"}}}
  ]
}

-- Dedicated (policy note) --
- Policies for dedicated clusters must be scoped to cluster-id and include "session_recording":"required" as a mandatory condition.

-- Private (operational note) --
- For private installs, policies are templates provided to customers; any Redwood-side service-account must be provisioned using the customer-approved SOW id and captured in activation evidence.

Monitoring and anomaly detection recommendations:
- Baseline JIT usage per team and alert for outliers (user requesting >3 JIT grants in 24h).
- Flag same activation_id reused across different requesters.
- High-risk signal: Approval chain missing security approver for high-risk scope -> immediate auto-escalation and session freeze.

Compliance and retention:
- Evidence artifacts retained for 7 years for enterprise customers; default 1 year for others unless legal hold.
- Evidence bucket lifecycle: immutable tier for 90 days after upload, then cold storage.

Operational runbooks (quick links):
- revoke-manual: steps to force-revoke a sticky entitlement (SSH session kill, policy detach, clear cache)
- review-process: templates for post-activation reviews and RCA

Open questions / TODOs:
- Finalize the exact canonical field name for approver set (approvers vs approver_primary).
- Decide whether to require signed approver justification for all high-risk activations.
- Integration work: Wire Evidence DB index into Observability for correlation with token-level cost / latency dashboards.

Appendix: example evidence record (single-line JSON for clarity):
{"activation_id":"6b8f5f2e-1f7c-4d8e-bb90-ae3c1c9f7f14","requester":"aisha.patel@redwood.ai","approvers":["marcus.nguyen@redwood.ai","sofia.hernandez@redwood.ai"],"role":"tenant-admin","scope":"tenant:acme-corp","host_tier":"dedicated","requested_duration_minutes":"240","issued_at":"2026-01-15T14:00:00Z","expires_at":"2026-01-15T18:00:00Z","justification":"urgent DB migration to apply security patch","runbook_link":"https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNBOOKS/DB-migration","evidence_refs":["s3://evidence/2026/01/6b8f5f2e-session-1.mp4"],"authorization_flow_id":"SEC-AUTH-412","automated_checks":["2fa_enabled","no_open_incidents"],"post_actions":["REV-2026-01-15-993"]}

Notes on uniqueness and provenance:
- This doc is intended to be the canonical Entitlement Activation Playbook for RBAC v2 activations, focused on evidence schema and SIEM export. It intentionally centralizes both policy and operational artifact requirements to make automation reliable for auditors.
